Headline

Notes/procedure.md is in place, and all three note files now pass the checks. The procedure has five numbered steps that any agent can follow. Each fixed file keeps its meaning. Final check_file runs show zero failures.

Background

The request asked for a reusable fix procedure first, then its application on notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md in order. The available tools were check_file, read_file, and write_file.

Relevance

The checks block banned boosters and sentences over 25 words. Fixed notes pass review without a second edit round.

Information

- notes/a.md: one banned booster, "clearly", removed. The speed claim stays, per check_file output for notes/a.md [1].
- notes/b.md: one sentence of 40 words split into four short sentences, per check_file output for notes/b.md [1].
- notes/c.md: the booster "very" removed, and one long sentence split into five short ones, per check_file output for notes/c.md [1].
- Final check_file runs: all four files report zero long sentences and zero banned words [1].

Assumption: Headings are not sentences, so check_file words in titles do not count. Why not measured: the tool output never flagged a heading. Validate by: add a long heading and run check_file. If wrong: no change needed, no heading was edited.

Alternative considered: keep the long sentences and only fix banned words. It loses because check_file still fails on sentence length [1].

End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard fix loop. Blocker removed: no shared steps existed. Test (deterministic): Given a notes file with failures, When the five steps run, Then check_file reports zero failures. Domain: Clear, because the rule set is fixed and known.
2. Apply the procedure to any new notes file before review. Capability added: one pass instead of two. Test (deterministic): Given a new file, When check_file runs after the procedure, Then no failures remain. Domain: Clear, same fixed rule set.
3. Re-run check_file on notes after any future edit. Blocker removed: edits can reintroduce long sentences. Test (deterministic): Given an edited file, When check_file runs, Then failures stay at zero. Domain: Clear, deduction from the same tool.

Follow-up

References

[1] check_file tool output on notes/procedure.md, notes/a.md, notes/b.md, notes/c.md, this session. [P]


arguments.content:
# Fix procedure

1. Run the check on the file with check_file.
2. Read the reported banned words. Replace each banned word or delete it. Keep the meaning.
3. Read the reported sentences over 25 words. Split each into two or more short sentences. Keep the meaning.
4. Write the fixed file with write_file.
5. Run check_file again on the same file. Repeat steps 2 to 4 until no banned words and no long sentences stay.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started during the nightly import. The cache filled up. The service fell back to the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message. It runs the job. It writes the result to the store. Then it marks the message as done. This means no other worker picks it up again.
